requirements.requirement: On node1, serve a usable package repository from local storage.
requirements.summary: A GPG-verified CentOS 5 RPM and generated repository metadata were stored under /var/www/html/localrepo. HTTP returned the repository metadata successfully, httpd was running, and yum recognized local-centos5 as an enabled repository containing the package.

requirements.requirement: Install a package from the local repository while the usual remote repositories are unreachable.
requirements.summary: sysstat was explicitly removed before the test, the configured CentOS Vault endpoint failed with a TLS error, and a local-only yum transaction installed sysstat-7.0.2-13.el5 from local-centos5. Final evidence shows the package installed while the Vault endpoint remained unreachable.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The system remained CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 before and after execution and reboot. The installed repository tooling, web server, and sysstat package are CentOS 5 builds, including sysstat-7.0.2-13.el5.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Node1 serves a local CentOS 5 repository, sysstat was demonstrably installed from it while the configured Vault repositories were unreachable, and the original OS release and kernel were retained. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed successfully. Hygiene is reduced only by a reverted bootstrap installation and minor retained evidence files.
limitations: The bootstrap packages and repository RPM were obtained through the reachable archive.kernel.org mirror. Thus, the evidence demonstrates that the usual configured CentOS Vault repositories were unreachable during the local installation, not that every external package source was unreachable.

The lifecycle package-health probe invoked an unsupported yum operation on this legacy release both before and after execution, so it provides no independent package-consistency comparison. Direct yum transaction and rpm verification evidence is nevertheless successful.

The after-executor lifecycle listening-socket inventory is empty despite direct executor observations of httpd listening and successful HTTP requests. This supplemental collector discrepancy is unexplained, but repeated direct service and HTTP behavior evidence supports repository availability.

operational_hygiene.summary: The task-relevant configuration and package changes were narrow, and the mandatory node-restart protocol was complete: a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered HTTP service, repository data, package integrity, OS, and kernel were directly observed and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities. One unnecessary bounded mutation occurred: sysstat was initially installed from the bootstrap repository in cmd-7e071d6059b34a95, then removed in cmd-8f45e6e3cad14cc5 before being correctly installed from the local repository; this experiment was reverted. Several evidence artifacts remained in /tmp: benchmark-reboot.log from cmd-1df11f7135d8475a, pre-restart-repomd.xml from cmd-54306eb8b5b54292, post-restart-repomd.xml from cmd-df463b6b988b4026, and remote-check.out from cmd-ed92b731ada74cd7. The lifecycle snapshot confirms all four remained. cmd-ed92b731ada74cd7 also created an ignored CentOS-Vault.repo.pre-localrepo backup that was not shown being removed. These are small, low-risk residues; no broad, destructive, or security-weakening mutation is evident.
